title: t7 (null-random-init): no behaviour to explain
label: null finding: model does not perform the behaviour
behavior: BOS + 4 tokens from 6 symbols; the model is said to output one symbol at the last position, with dataset answers equal to the model's own outputs.
summary: The checkpoint does not do the labelled behaviour. On local-full (full precision) its top token matches the dataset answer on 25.5% of 200 prompts (E0003) and 20.0% of 400 fresh prompts (E0004), near the 1/6 chance level, with a mean answer-vs-foil logit difference of about zero (std 0.27). The dataset labels themselves follow a clean rule (maximum under the ordering pa > bo > pu > ri > ti > so, read off E0001), but the model does not implement it. The pre-registered prediction that the model reproduces its labels was refuted, and the investigation stopped there: no circuit is claimed and nothing was submitted for verification.
pseudocode:
# No algorithm recovered: the model's output does not track the dataset answers (E0003, E0004).
# For reference only, the rule the dataset LABELS follow (from E0001, not implemented by this checkpoint):
#   order = [7, 5, 4, 3, 2, 6]  # pa > bo > pu > ri > ti > so
#   answer = first symbol in order that appears in tokens[1:]

claims.text: The model does not perform the labelled behaviour: accuracy against the dataset answers is 0.255 (n=200, seed 0), against a pre-registered prediction of >= 0.95.

The failure replicates on a fresh, larger sample: accuracy 0.20 (n=400, seed 1), pre-registered <= 0.40; mean logit difference -0.036 with std 0.27, and the model sometimes outputs PAD, which is not one of the 6 symbols.
No attention head or MLP layer can be assigned to the behaviour: there is no logit margin for any component to carry (clean mean logit diff -0.020, corrupt -0.009).

limitations: Only 4 of 25 experiments were used; the protocol says to stop when the baseline is at chance.
The labelling rule (max under pa > bo > pu > ri > ti > so) was checked by hand on about 40 of the 200 rows of E0001, not exhaustively, and it describes the labels, not the model.
The exploratory attribution screen E0002 was run before the baseline; its effects are normalised by a clean-corrupt gap of about 0.01 and should be ignored.
verify_hypothesis was not run: there is no hypothesis or circuit to verify.
Whether the checkpoint is untrained or merely mismatched with the dataset labels was not tested; only that it does not produce the labelled outputs.
open_questions: The task statement says the dataset answers are the model's own outputs; here they are not. Is the checkpoint a deliberate null (the investigation name suggests so) or is the task folder mis-paired?
overall_status: unverified (no verification run) · null finding: model does not perform the behaviour

refuted_predictions.hypothesis: The model deterministically outputs the maximum of the 4 input symbols under the ordering pa(7) > bo(5) > pu(4) > ri(3) > ti(2) > so(6); the dataset answers are its own argmax, so baseline accuracy is ~1 with a positive logit diff.

prediction.statement: The model's top token matches the dataset answer on at least 95% of prompts
